speaker: Doctor
text: That is a very important question. Have you noticed any changes in your speech, swallowing, or facial muscles? Also, please tell me if you experience any drooping eyelids or blurred vision that comes and goes.

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis. The combination of fluctuating ocular symptoms (double vision on gaze), limb weakness that worsens with exertion and improves with rest, and the absence of sensory deficits or balance issues is highly characteristic of this condition. I recommend confirming this with a Tensilon test and checking for thymoma via CT Chest. REQUEST TEST: Anti-AChR Antibodies; REQUEST TEST: CT_Chest.
